title: Where Does the Signal Live? A Web Data Recipe for Medical Encoder Pretraining
abstract: arXiv:2606.22079v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Web data curation has been widely studied for decoder Large Language Model (LLM) pretraining. Encoders for dense-terminology domains such as medicine, by contrast, are pretrained on small, manually-curated corpora that limit scalability and writing style diversity, a bottleneck even more severe in non-English clinical settings. Whether web-scale data curation also benefits encoder Masked Language Modeling (MLM) in a dense-terminology domain remains an open question. To address this, we introduce two complementary levers. Medical-term density filtering selects documents rich in medical terms. Signal-amplifying rephrasing uses an LLM to rewrite documents into denser variants with broader entity contexts. We instantiate the recipe on French medical NLP. The medical-term density filter outperforms the widely-used educational quality filter on downstream medical tasks, and the two complement each other. Signal-amplifying rephrasing

translated_title: 信号藏在哪里？一种用于医学编码器预训练的网络数据配方
translated_abstract: 网络数据策划已被广泛研究用于解码器大语言模型（LLM）的预训练。相比之下，医学等密集术语领域的编码器通常在小型、人工策划的语料库上进行预训练，这限制了可扩展性和写作风格的多样性，而这一瓶颈在非英语临床环境中更为严重。网络规模的数据策划是否也能使密集术语领域的编码器掩码语言建模（MLM）受益，仍然是一个悬而未决的问题。为了解决这个问题，我们引入了两个互补的杠杆：医学术语密度过滤，用于选择富含医学术语的文档；信号放大改写，使用LLM将文档改写为术语更密集且实体上下文更广泛的变体。我们在法语医学NLP上实例化了该配方。结果表明，医学术语密度过滤器在下游医学任务上优于广泛使用的教育质量过滤器，且二者互补。信号放大改写…
tldr: 该论文提出了一种面向医学编码器预训练的网络数据配方，通过医学术语密度过滤与LLM信号放大改写两种互补策略，在法语医学NLP任务上超越了广泛使用的教育质量过滤方法。
